U.S. Census Bureau 2024 Gazetteer (map location)
EFF Atlas of Surveillance (police surveillance technology, searched by department)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended November 30, 2024, as the county reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Illinois Comptroller. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. The county collector gathers property taxes for every taxing district and pays them over; that money is left out.

Covers the general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service and enterprise (utility) funds. Pension trusts and other fiduciary funds, internal service funds and component units are left out, as are transfers between funds and borrowing.
Capital outlay outside utility funds ($563,176) is reported without a function, so it is spread over the county's services in proportion to their spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, contracts and other long-term debt outstanding at year end (beginning balance plus new debt less debt retired), as reported.
Political money is not scored: no county board and county office candidates of Schuyler County reported contributions to the State Board of Elections since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Illinois yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
